title.en: Volume 67 Book of Later Tang 43: Biographies 19 - Dou Luge, Wei Shou, Lu Cheng, Zhao Feng, Li Yu, Ren Huan
title.raw: 卷六十七 唐書43: 列傳19 豆盧革 韋說 盧程 趙鳳 李愚 任圜 Volume 67 Book of Later Tang 43: Biographies 19 - Dou Luge, Wei Shou, Lu Cheng, Zhao Feng, Li Yu, Ren Huan

sentences.zh: 豆盧革，祖籍，同州刺史。

translations.literal: Dou Luge — [his] ancestral lineage [is not recorded]. [A forebear served as] Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge came of a house whose pedigree is lost to the record; a forebear had held the prefecture of Tong.

sentences.zh: 父瓚，舒州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zan served as Prefect of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zan had been prefect of Shu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: （《宣和書譜》云：失其世係。）〉

translations.literal: (The Xuande Calligraphy Catalogue states that his genealogical line was lost.))
translations.idiomatic: (The Xuande Calligraphy Catalogue notes that his family line was lost.))

sentences.zh: 革少值亂離，避地鄜、延，轉入中山，王處直禮之，辟於幕下，有奏記之譽。

translations.literal: In his youth Ge encountered turmoil and displacement, fleeing to Fu and Yan, then moving into Zhongshan; Wang Chuzhi treated him with courtesy, recruited him to his staff, and he gained a reputation for memorial writing.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Ge lived through chaos and exile, taking refuge in Fu and Yan before settling in Zhongshan, where Wang Chuzhi honored him, brought him onto his staff, and he won renown for his memorials.

sentences.zh: 因牡丹會賦詩，諷處直以桑柘為意，言甚古雅，漸加器仰，轉節度判官。

translations.literal: At a peony gathering he composed a poem, admonishing Chuzhi with mulberry and catalpa as his theme; his language was very antique in style, and Chuzhi gradually came to esteem him, promoting him to military commissioner adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: At a peony festival he wrote a poem urging Chuzhi to heed the mulberry and catalpa—the staple crops of the people—in elegantly archaic verse; Chuzhi grew to admire him and made him adjutant to the military governor.

sentences.zh: 而理家無法，獨請謁處直，處直慮布政有缺，有所規諫，斂版出迎，乃為嬖人祈軍職矣。

translations.literal: Yet in managing his household he had no discipline; he alone requested an audience with Chuzhi. Chuzhi, fearing lapses in his governance, offered remonstrance; Ge folded his tablet and came out to receive him—only to seek a military post for a favorite.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he ran his household without order and went alone to see Chuzhi. When Chuzhi, worried about flaws in his administration, tried to counsel him, Ge put away his tablet and came out to greet him—only to ask a military commission for a favorite.

sentences.zh: 天祐末，莊宗將即位，講求輔相，盧質以名家子舉之，征拜行台左丞相。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianyou era, as Emperor Zhuangzong was about to take the throne, he sought chief ministers; Lu Zhi recommended him as a son of an eminent house, and he was summoned and appointed Left Chancellor of the Mobile Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Tianyou, as Zhuangzong prepared to ascend the throne and searched for chief ministers, Lu Zhi nominated him as a scion of a great clan, and he was called to serve as Left Chancellor of the Mobile Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 同光初，拜平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang, he was appointed Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening year of Tongguang he was made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 及登廊廟，事多錯亂，至於官階擬議，前後倒置，屢為省郎蕭希甫駿正，革改之，無難色。

translations.literal: Once he entered the hall of state, affairs were often in disorder; even in proposing official ranks, precedence was reversed front and back. He was repeatedly corrected by Secretariat officer Xiao Xifu; Ge amended his proposals without displeasure.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached the council chamber, business was often confused—even rank proposals were put in the wrong order—and Secretariat officer Xiao Xifu had to correct him again and again; Ge changed his drafts without taking offense.

sentences.zh: 莊宗初定汴、洛，革引薦韋說，冀諳事體，與己同功。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong first secured Bian and Luo, Ge recommended Wei Shuo, hoping he would understand affairs of state and share the work with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong first secured Bian and Luoyang, Ge recommended Wei Shuo, expecting someone who understood government to share the burden with him.

sentences.zh: 說既登庸，復事流品，舉止輕脫，怨歸於革。

translations.literal: Once Shuo took office, he again busied himself with pedigree and rank; his conduct was frivolous, and resentment fell on Ge.
translations.idiomatic: After Shuo took office he again obsessed over pedigree and rank, behaved with careless levity, and public blame settled on Ge.

sentences.zh: 又革、說之子俱授拾遺，父子同官，為人所刺，遂改授員外郎。

translations.literal: Moreover, both Ge's and Shuo's sons were appointed Remonstrance Officials; father and son held office together, which people criticized, so they were reassigned as Vice Directors.
translations.idiomatic: Both men's sons were also made Remonstrance Officials—fathers and sons serving together—which drew sharp criticism, and the appointments were changed to outside-director posts.

sentences.zh: 革請說之子濤為宏文館學士，說請革之子升為集賢學士，交易市恩，有同市井，識者醜之。

translations.literal: Ge requested Shuo's son Tao as Academician of the Hongwen Institute; Shuo requested Ge's son Sheng as Academician of the Jixian Institute—trading favors like hucksters in the marketplace; the discerning were disgusted.
translations.idiomatic: Ge secured Shuo's son Tao a post at the Hongwen Institute while Shuo secured Ge's son Sheng one at Jixian—bartering patronage like market traders, to the revulsion of anyone with judgment.

sentences.zh: 革自作相之後，不以進賢勸能為務，唯事修煉，求長生之術；

translations.literal: After Ge became chief minister himself, he did not make promoting the worthy and encouraging talent his task, but devoted himself only to cultivation and sought the art of long life;
translations.idiomatic: Once Ge was chief minister himself, he no longer troubled to advance the worthy or encourage ability, but devoted himself to alchemical cultivation in search of immortality;

sentences.zh: 嘗服丹砂，嘔血數日，垂死而愈。

translations.literal: He once took cinnabar and vomited blood for several days, nearly dying before he recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He once ingested cinnabar, spat blood for days, and was near death before he recovered.

sentences.zh: 天成初，將葬莊宗，以革為山陵使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng, as Zhuangzong was to be buried, Ge was made Commissioner for the Imperial Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng, when Zhuangzong was to be interred, Ge was appointed commissioner for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 及木主歸廟，不出私第，專俟旄鎮，數日無耗，為親友促令入朝。

translations.literal: When the spirit tablet returned to the ancestral temple, he did not leave his private residence, but waited solely for a frontier commission; for several days there was no word, and relatives and friends urged him to attend court.
translations.idiomatic: After the spirit tablet was installed in the temple he stayed home, waiting only for a border governorship; when days passed without news, friends pressed him to go to court.

sentences.zh: 安重誨對眾辱之曰：「山陵使名銜尚在，不候新命，便履公朝，意謂邊人可欺也。

translations.literal: An Chonghui publicly humiliated him, saying: "The title of Mausoleum Commissioner is still on you; without awaiting a new appointment you tread the public court—do you think men of the frontier may be deceived?"
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui shamed him before the assembly: "You still bear the title of Mausoleum Commissioner. You enter the public court without waiting for a new appointment—as if frontier men were fools to be tricked."

sentences.zh: 」側目者聞之，思有所中。

translations.literal: " Those who watched with sidelong glances heard this and thought to strike at him.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who had long watched him with envy heard this and looked for a chance to bring him down.

sentences.zh: 初，蕭希甫有正諫之望，革嘗阻之，遂上疏論革與說苟且自容，致君無狀。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xiao Xifu had hopes of upright remonstrance; Ge had once blocked him, so he submitted a memorial accusing Ge and Shuo of making shift to preserve themselves and treating the ruler without proper form.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xifu had once hoped to serve as a forthright remonstrator, but Ge had blocked him; he now memorialized that Ge and Shuo were self-serving survivors who had disgraced their service to the throne.

sentences.zh: 復誣其縱田客殺人，冒元亨上第。

translations.literal: He further accused him of letting tenant farmers kill people and of fraudulently taking top rank in the Yuanheng examination.
translations.idiomatic: He further charged that Ge had allowed estate tenants to commit murder and had falsely claimed top honors in the Yuanheng examinations.

sentences.zh: 遂貶為辰州刺史，仍令所在馳驛發遣。

translations.literal: He was then demoted to Prefect of Chen Prefecture, and orders were sent for express relay posts to dispatch him.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was demoted to prefect of Chen and ordered sent off at once by relay post.

sentences.zh: 後鄭玨、任圜等連上三章，請不行後命，乃下製曰：「豆盧革、韋說等，身為輔相，手握權衡，或端坐稱臣，或半笑奏事，於君無禮，舉世寧容。

translations.literal: Later Zheng Jue, Ren Huan, and others submitted three successive memorials asking that the later order not be carried out; then an edict was issued: "Dou Luge, Wei Shuo, and the like, serving as chief ministers and holding the scales of power, either sat upright addressing themselves as subjects or reported affairs with half a smile—toward their ruler without propriety; could the world tolerate them?"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jue, Ren Huan, and others then submitted three memorials asking that the harsher sentence be set aside; the throne replied by edict: "Dou Luge, Wei Shuo, and their kind held the chief ministry and the scales of power, yet addressed the throne either with stiff formality or with an insolent half-smile—conduct no ruler could abide and no age could excuse."

sentences.zh: 革則暫委利權，便私俸祿，文武百辟皆從五月起支，父子二人偏自正初給遣。

translations.literal: As for Ge, he briefly delegated profitable authority and then privatized salaries: all civil and military officials were paid from the fifth month onward, while father and son alone were supplied from the first month of the year.
translations.idiomatic: Ge had briefly handed off lucrative power only to seize salaries for himself: every other official was paid from the fifth month, while he and his son drew pay from the first.

sentences.zh: 說則自居重位，全紊大綱。

translations.literal: Shuo, for his part, occupied a weighty post and wholly disordered the great framework.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo, holding high office, had thrown the whole administrative order into confusion.

sentences.zh: 敘蔭貪榮，亂兒孫於昭穆；

translations.literal: recording inherited privilege out of greed for glory, disordering sons and grandsons in the ancestral order;
translations.idiomatic: greedily trading inherited privilege for rank, scrambling the proper order of descent in the ancestral halls;

sentences.zh: 賣官潤屋，換令錄之身名。

translations.literal: selling offices to enrich their houses, trading magistrate and registrar posts for personal names.
translations.idiomatic: selling offices to fatten their households, bartering prefectural and registrar posts for private gain.

sentences.zh: 醜行疊彰，群情共怒，雖居牧守，示塞非尤。

translations.literal: Ugly conduct piled up layer on layer; public sentiment raged together. Though they were placed in prefectural governorships, this showed that blame was not being stuffed away.
translations.idiomatic: Their disgrace multiplied and public wrath united; even assigning them prefectures would not bury the outrage.

sentences.zh: 革可責授費州司戶參軍，說可夷州司戶參軍，皆員外置同正員，並所在馳驛發遣。

translations.literal: Ge is demoted to Revenue Section Army Adjutant of Fei Prefecture; Shuo to Revenue Section Army Adjutant of Yi Prefecture—both extra appointees with the status of regular incumbents—and both are to be dispatched by express relay wherever they are.
translations.idiomatic: Ge is stripped to Revenue Section adjutant at Fei, Shuo to the same rank at Yi—outside appointments with nominal full status—and both are to be hustled off by relay post.

sentences.zh: 」尋貶陵州長流百姓，委長吏常知所在。

translations.literal: " Soon they were further demoted to exiled commoners at Ling Prefecture, with local chief officials charged always to know their whereabouts.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon both were banished as common exiles to Ling, with local authorities ordered to keep constant track of them.

sentences.zh: 天成二年夏，詔令逐處刺史監賜自盡，其骨肉並放逐便。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Tiancheng, an edict ordered prefects everywhere to supervise and grant them death by their own hand; their kin were also to be exiled as convenient.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Tiancheng 2 an edict commanded every prefect to oversee their compelled suicide, and their families were to be exiled forthwith.

sentences.zh: 子升，官至檢校正郎，服金紫，尋亦削奪。

translations.literal: His son Sheng reached the post of Regular Rectifying Gentleman, wore gold and purple, and soon lost these as well.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng had risen to Regular Rectifying Gentleman and worn gold and purple insignia, but soon lost both.

sentences.zh: （《寶晉齋法書讚》載豆盧革《田園帖》云：大德欲要一居處，畿甸間舊無田園，鄜州雖有三兩處莊子，緣百姓租佃多年，累有令公大王書請，卻給還人戶，蓋不欲侵奪疲民，兼慮無知之輩，妄有影庇包役云云。

translations.literal: (Baojin Studio's Calligraphy Eulogies records Dou Luge's "Estate Letter," which says: "Great Virtue wishes to have a residence. Around the capital district I formerly had no estate. Although Fu Prefecture has two or three manor farms, because the common people have rented and tilled them for many years, and the Lord Prince has repeatedly written requesting them, I have returned them to the households—lest weary people be seized upon, and lest ignorant persons falsely shelter others to evade corvée, and so forth."
translations.idiomatic: (Baojin Studio's Calligraphy Eulogies preserves Ge's "Estate Letter," in which he writes that he needed a home near the capital but owned no land there; though Fu had a few manors, tenants had farmed them for years and the "Lord Prince" had repeatedly demanded them back, so he returned the holdings rather than prey on exhausted commoners or let the ignorant use false patronage to dodge labor obligations."

sentences.zh: 嶽珂曰：此帖乃與僧往還書，其畏強藩避罪罟，蓋栗栗淵冰，然其後卒以故縱田客貶夜郎，正坐所畏，信乎亂邦之不可居也。

translations.literal: Yue Ke says: This letter is correspondence with a monk. His fear of powerful frontier lords and avoidance of the net of guilt were like treading on thin ice over a deep abyss; yet afterward he was finally banished to Yelang for deliberately indulging tenant farmers—exactly what he had feared. Truly a chaotic state is no place to dwell.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Ke comments that the letter was exchanged with a monk: Ge's dread of powerful regional lords and of the law's snare was like walking on ice above an abyss—yet he was later exiled to Yelang for indulging estate tenants, punished for the very danger he had tried to evade; a chaotic age, indeed, was no home for an honest man.

sentences.zh: 是時據鄜乃高萬興，官檢校太師、中書令，封北平王，即革所謂「令公大王」者。

translations.literal: At that time the holder of Fu was Gao Wanxing, whose offices were Acting Grand Preceptor and Director of the Secretariat, enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping—the very "Lord Prince" of whom Ge spoke.
translations.idiomatic: Fu was then held by Gao Wanxing, Acting Grand Preceptor and Secretariat Director, enfeoffed as Prince of Beiping—the "Lord Prince" Ge meant in the letter.

sentences.zh: 官故梁授，唐命維新，而顓麵正朝者，不能致褫鞶之誅，而反竊貢秉旄之佞，唐之不競，有自來矣。）〉

translations.literal: His offices were old appointments from Liang; Tang's mandate was renewed, yet those who faced the proper court could not bring down the punishment of stripping his regalia, but instead secretly accepted his tribute and the flattery of one who bore the staff of command—Tang's lack of vigor had long had its causes.))
translations.idiomatic: His titles were leftovers from Liang, while Tang had only just renewed the mandate; yet the court that faced him could not strip his honors, and instead took his gifts and the sycophancy of a man clutching a commander's staff—Tang's weakness, it seems, was nothing new.))

sentences.zh: 韋說，福建觀察使岫之子也。

translations.literal: Wei Shuo was the son of Xu, Military Governor of Fujian Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Shuo was the son of Xu, commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: （案：以下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: There is missing text below.))
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Text is missing below.))

sentences.zh: 莊宗定汴、洛，說與趙光允同製拜平章事。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong secured Bian and Luo, Shuo and Zhao Guangyun were jointly appointed by edict as Grand Councillors.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhuangzong secured Bian and Luoyang, Shuo and Zhao Guangyun were appointed Grand Councillors by the same edict.

sentences.zh: 說性謹重，奉職常不造事端。

translations.literal: Shuo's nature was cautious and grave; in office he ordinarily stirred up no incidents.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo was cautious and sober by nature and usually made no trouble in office.

sentences.zh: 時郭崇韜秉政，說等承順而已，政事得失，無所措言。

translations.literal: At the time Guo Chongtao held power; Shuo and the others merely complied, with nowhere to speak on the gains and losses of government.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chongtao then dominated government; Shuo and his colleagues only assented and had no voice in policy right or wrong.

sentences.zh: 初，或有言於崇韜，銓選逾濫，選人或取他人出身銜，或取父兄資緒，與令史囊橐罔冒，崇韜乃條奏其事。

translations.literal: Earlier, someone told Chongtao that selection and appointment had grown excessive: candidates took others' origin credentials, or borrowed fathers' and brothers' seniority, colluding with clerks in bribery and false claims; Chongtao then submitted a detailed memorial on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Someone had told Chongtao that appointments had grown corrupt—candidates using others' credentials or their fathers' seniority while clerks took bribes—and Chongtao memorialized the abuses in detail.

sentences.zh: 其後郊天，行事官數千人，多有告敕偽濫，因定去留，塗毀告身者甚眾，選人號哭都門之外。

translations.literal: Afterward, at the suburban sacrifice to Heaven, several thousand participating officials were found in many cases to have forged or spurious appointment documents; retention and dismissal were decided accordingly, and very many had their credentials defaced—candidates wailed outside the capital gates.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the suburban sacrifice, thousands of ritual officers were found with forged commissions; as keepers and dismissals were decided, credentials were crossed out in great numbers and rejected candidates wept outside the capital gates.

sentences.zh: 議者亦以為積弊累年，一旦澄汰太細，懼失惟新含垢之意。

translations.literal: Commentators also held that abuses had accumulated for years, and to clarify and purge too finely in a single stroke feared losing the intent of renewal that bears with grime.
translations.idiomatic: Critics argued that years of rot could not be purged in one ruthless sweep without betraying the new reign's promise of forbearance.

sentences.zh: 時說與郭崇韜國列，不能執而止之，頗遭物議。

translations.literal: At the time Shuo held equal rank with Guo Chongtao in the state hierarchy and could not hold fast and stop it, and he suffered considerable public criticism.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo then ranked with Guo Chongtao in the state hierarchy yet could not restrain him, and public opinion turned sharply against him.

sentences.zh: 說之親黨告之，說曰：「此郭漢子之意也。

translations.literal: Shuo's kin and associates informed him; Shuo said: "This is that Guo fellow's idea."
translations.idiomatic: When kinsmen warned him, Shuo said, "This is that Guo fellow's doing."

sentences.zh: 」及崇韜得罪，說懼流言所鍾，乃令門人左拾遺王鬆、吏部員外郎李慎儀等上疏，云：「崇韜往日專權，不閑故實，塞仕進之門，非獎善之道。

translations.literal: " When Chongtao fell from grace, Shuo feared slander would converge on him and had his protégés—Left Remonstrance Official Wang Song and Vice Director of Personnel Li Shenyi—submit a memorial saying: "Chongtao in the past monopolized power, was unversed in precedent, blocked the gates of advancement, and this is not the way to reward goodness."
translations.idiomatic: " After Chongtao fell, Shuo feared the backlash would engulf him and had his protégés Wang Song and Li Shenyi memorialize that Chongtao had monopolized power, ignored precedent, and blocked the path of merit—no way to reward the worthy.

sentences.zh: 」疏下中書，說等覆奏，深詆崇韜，識者非之。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the Secretariat; Shuo and others replied in memorial, deeply denouncing Chongtao; the discerning disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: " When the memorial reached the Secretariat, Shuo and his circle replied with a still harsher attack on Chongtao, which men of judgment condemned.

sentences.zh: 又有王傪者，能以多岐取事，納賂於說，說以其名犯祖諱，遂改之為「操」，擬官於近甸。

translations.literal: There was also one Wang Can, who could gain affairs by many crooked paths and offered bribes to Shuo; Shuo, because his name violated an ancestral taboo, changed it to "Cao" and proposed an office for him in the near capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: A man named Wang Can, skilled at working every angle, bribed Shuo; Shuo, claiming the name violated a taboo, changed it to Cao and arranged a post for him near the capital.

sentences.zh: 及明宗即位，說常慮身危，每求庇於任圜，常保護之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Mingzong took the throne, Shuo often feared for his person and repeatedly sought protection from Ren Huan, who regularly shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: After Mingzong ascended the throne, Shuo lived in fear for his life and repeatedly sought Ren Huan's protection, which Ren usually gave.

sentences.zh: 說居有井，昔與鄰家共之，因嫌鄙雜，築垣於外。

translations.literal: Shuo's residence had a well, formerly shared with neighbors; disliking their vulgar crowding, he built a wall outside.
translations.idiomatic: Shuo's house had a well once shared with neighbors; finding them coarse and intrusive, he walled it off from the street.

sentences.zh: 鄰人訟之，為希甫疏論，以為井有貨財，及案之本人，惟稱有破釜一所，反招虛妄。

translations.literal: The neighbors sued; Xifu memorialized against him, claiming the well held valuables; when the case was investigated, Shuo himself said only that there was one broken cauldron—thus inviting the charge of falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: The neighbors sued; Xifu accused him of hoarding valuables in the well, but when the case was examined Shuo could point only to a broken pot—exposing the charge as fabrication.

sentences.zh: 初貶敘州刺史，尋責授夷州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: He was first demoted to Prefect of Xu Prefecture, then stripped and appointed Revenue Section Army Adjutant of Yi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was first demoted to prefect of Xu, then reduced to revenue adjutant at Yi.

sentences.zh: 初，說在江陵，與高季興相知，及入中書，亦常通信幣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shuo was at Jiangling, he was acquainted with Gao Jixing; after entering the Secretariat, he also often exchanged gifts and letters.
translations.idiomatic: While Shuo was at Jiangling he had known Gao Jixing, and after joining the Secretariat he continued to exchange gifts and correspondence.

sentences.zh: 自討西蜀，季興請攻峽內，莊宗許之：「如能得三州，俾為屬郡。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Western Shu began, Jixing requested to attack the inner gorges; Zhuangzong assented: "If you can take the three prefectures, they shall be made your subordinate commanderies."
translations.idiomatic: During the western Shu campaign Jixing asked to strike the gorge region; Zhuangzong agreed: "If you take the three prefectures, they shall be yours as subordinate districts."

sentences.zh: 」西川既定，季興無尺寸之功。

translations.literal: " Western Shu was pacified, but Jixing had not a foot of achievement.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu was pacified, yet Jixing had won not a foot of ground.

sentences.zh: 洎明宗纘承，季興頻請三郡，朝廷不得已而與之。

translations.literal: By the time Mingzong succeeded, Jixing repeatedly requested the three commanderies, and the court, having no choice, granted them.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong succeeded the throne, Jixing pressed repeatedly for the three districts, and the court reluctantly yielded.

sentences.zh: 革、說方在中書，亦預其議。

translations.literal: Ge and Shuo were then in the Secretariat and also took part in the deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Ge and Shuo were then in the Secretariat and took part in the decision.

sentences.zh: 及季興占據，獨歸其罪，流於合州。

translations.literal: When Jixing seized and held them, the blame was placed on them alone, and they were exiled to He Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Jixing kept the territories, blame fell on them alone and they were exiled to He.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，詔曰：「陵州、合州長流百姓豆盧革、韋說，頃在先朝，擢居重任，欺公害物，黷貨賣官。

translations.literal: The next summer an edict said: "The exiled commoners Dou Luge at Ling Prefecture and Wei Shuo at He Prefecture were lately raised to heavy responsibility under the former court, harmed the public and preyed on things, took bribes and sold offices."
translations.idiomatic: The following summer an edict declared: "The exiles Dou Luge at Ling and Wei Shuo at He were lately elevated to high office under the former emperor, yet harmed the realm, preyed on the people, and sold offices for bribes."

sentences.zh: 靜惟肇亂之端，更有難容之事，且夔、忠、萬三州，地連巴蜀，路扼荊蠻，藉皇都弭難之初，徇逆帥僭求之勢，罔予視聽，率意割移。

translations.literal: Quietly considering the source of disorder, there were further acts hard to tolerate: moreover, the three prefectures of Kui, Zhong, and Wan border Ba and Shu and choke the routes of Jing and the southern tribes; relying on the capital's first effort to quell trouble, they indulged a rebellious commander's presumptuous demands, disregarded Our sight and hearing, and willfully ceded and transferred territory.
translations.idiomatic: Worse still were acts that could not be borne: Kui, Zhong, and Wan lie against Ba-Shu and guard the routes into Jing and the south; at the very hour the capital was settling turmoil they indulged a rebel commander's brazen demands, ignored the throne, and casually ceded territory.

sentences.zh: 將千之土疆，開通狡穴；

translations.literal: a thousand li of territory about to be opened to cunning lairs;
translations.idiomatic: a thousand li of frontier about to be opened to enemy lairs;

sentences.zh: 動兩川之兵賦，禦捍經年。

translations.literal: mobilizing the armies and levies of the Two Shu, defending for years on end.
translations.idiomatic: forcing the Two Shu to mobilize troops and taxes in defense year after year.

sentences.zh: 致朕莫遂偃戈，猶煩運策。

translations.literal: causing Us not yet to lay down arms, still troubled with planning campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: so that We could not yet sheathe the sword but still had to scheme for war.

sentences.zh: 近者西方鄴雖復要害，高季興尚固窠巢，增吾旰食之憂，職爾朋奸之計。

translations.literal: Lately, though Ye in the west has been recovered as a strategic point, Gao Jixing still holds fast to his lair, increasing Our worry that steals sleep from meals—owing to your faction's treacherous designs.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ye on the western front has lately been recovered, Jixing still clings to his nest, deepening Our sleepless worry—thanks to your faction's scheming.

sentences.zh: 而又自居貶所，繼出流言。

translations.literal: Moreover, while dwelling in your place of demotion, you have continued to spread slander.
translations.idiomatic: And from your places of exile you have kept spreading slander.

sentences.zh: 苟刑戮之稽時，處忠良於何地？

translations.literal: If punishment and execution are delayed in time, where are the loyal and good to be placed?
translations.idiomatic: If punishment is long delayed, what place remains for the loyal?

sentences.zh: 宜令逐處刺史監賜自盡。」

translations.literal: It is fitting to order prefects everywhere to supervise and grant them death by their own hand."
translations.idiomatic: Let every prefect oversee their compelled suicide."

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》：說子濤，晉天福初，為尚書膳部員外郎，卒。）〉

translations.literal: (Ouyang's History: Shuo's son Tao, at the beginning of Jin Tianfu, was Vice Director of Provisions in the Ministry of Revenue and died.))
translations.idiomatic: (Ouyang's History notes that Shuo's son Tao served as Vice Director of Provisions under Jin in the early Tianfu era and died.))

sentences.zh: 盧程，唐朝右族。

translations.literal: Lu Cheng was of a great Tang clan on the right.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng came of a leading Tang clan.

sentences.zh: 祖懿，父蘊，曆仕通顯。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi and father Yun both served through prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi and father Yun had both risen to eminent office.

sentences.zh: 程，天復末登進士第，崔魏公領鹽鐵，署為巡官。

translations.literal: Cheng, at the end of Tianfu passed the jinshi examination; when Duke Cui of Wei headed the Salt and Iron Commission, he appointed him touring officer.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng passed the jinshi late in Tianfu; when Cui Yin headed the Salt and Iron Commission he made him a touring officer.

sentences.zh: 昭宗遷洛陽，柳璨陷右族，程避地河朔，客遊燕、趙，或衣道士服，幹謁藩伯，人未知之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved to Luoyang, Liu Can entrapped the great clans of the right; Cheng fled to the north of the Yellow River, traveled as a guest through Yan and Zhao, sometimes wearing Taoist robes and importuning frontier lords—people did not know him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong moved the court to Luoyang and Liu Can persecuted the great families, Cheng fled to Hebei, wandered as a guest through Yan and Zhao, sometimes in Taoist dress importuning regional lords, unknown to all.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革客遊中山，依王處直，盧汝弼來太原。

translations.literal: Dou Luge traveled as a guest in Zhongshan and relied on Wang Chuzhi; Lu Rubi came to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge was then a guest in Zhongshan under Wang Chuzhi, and Lu Rubi had come to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 程與革、弼皆朝族知舊，因往來依革，處直禮遇未優，故投於太原；

translations.literal: Cheng, Ge, and Bi were all court-clan acquaintances of old; he therefore went back and forth relying on Ge. Chuzhi's courtesy was not generous, so he turned to Taiyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng, Ge, and Bi were old friends among the capital elite; Cheng attached himself to Ge, but Chuzhi treated him poorly, so he went to Taiyuan;

sentences.zh: 汝弼因為延譽，莊宗署為推官，尋改支使。

translations.literal: Rubi thereupon recommended him; Zhuangzong appointed him investigating officer, soon changed to staff adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Rubi recommended him; Zhuangzong made him investigating officer, then staff adjutant.

sentences.zh: 程褊淺無他才，惟矜恃門第，口多是非，篤厚君子尤薄之。

translations.literal: Cheng was narrow and shallow, without other talent, relying only on his pedigree, his mouth full of right and wrong; earnest and generous gentlemen especially despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was shallow and talentless, proud only of birth, and full of gossip; men of real substance despised him.

sentences.zh: 初，判官王緘從軍掌文翰，胡柳之役，緘歿於軍。

translations.literal: Earlier, adjutant Wang Jian followed the army managing documents; in the battle at Huliu, Jian died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Adjutant Wang Jian had managed the army's paperwork; he was killed at Huliu.

sentences.zh: 莊宗歸寧太原，置酒公宴，舉酒謂張承業曰：「予今於此會取一書記，先以卮酒辟之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong returned to pay respects at Taiyuan and set out wine for a public banquet; raising his cup he said to Zhang Chengye: "I shall now at this gathering choose a secretary; first let this cup of wine declare it."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong returned to Taiyuan for a family visit he held a public feast and told Zhang Chengye, raising his cup: "Tonight I shall choose a secretary—let this cup announce it."

sentences.zh: 」即舉酒屬巡官馮道，道以所舉非次，抗酒辭避。

translations.literal: " He then raised his cup toward touring officer Feng Dao; Dao, because the nomination was out of order, resisted the wine and declined.
translations.idiomatic: " He turned to touring officer Feng Dao; Dao, saying the choice skipped proper order, refused the cup.

sentences.zh: 莊宗曰：「勿謙挹，無逾於卿也。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said: "Do not be modest—none surpasses you."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong said, "Do not demur—no one is better suited."

sentences.zh: 」時以職列序遷，則程當為書記，汝弼亦左右之。

translations.literal: " At the time, by order of rank in office, Cheng ought to have been secretary, and Rubi also urged it.
translations.idiomatic: " By seniority Cheng should have been secretary, and Rubi had been pressing for him.

sentences.zh: 程既失職，私懷憤惋，謂人曰：「主上不重人物，使田里兒居餘上。

translations.literal: Cheng having lost the post, privately harbored resentment and said to others: "Our lord does not value men of quality, letting a village lad sit above me."
translations.idiomatic: Denied the post, Cheng nursed private resentment and told others, "The ruler cares nothing for talent, setting a village upstart above me."

sentences.zh: 」先是，莊宗嘗於帳中召程草奏，程曰：「叨忝成名，不閑筆硯。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Zhuangzong had once summoned Cheng in the tent to draft a memorial; Cheng said: "I have undeservedly achieved fame and am unskilled with brush and inkstone."
translations.idiomatic: " Earlier Zhuangzong had asked him to draft a memorial in camp; Cheng replied, "I am unworthy of my fame and no hand at writing."

sentences.zh: 」由是文翰之選，不及於程。

translations.literal: " From this, choice for literary posts did not reach Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: " After that he was never considered for literary office.

sentences.zh: 時張承業專製河東留守事，人皆敬憚。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Chengye monopolized control of the Hedong rear-presidency affairs, and all men respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chengye then controlled Hedong as rear-president, and everyone feared him.

sentences.zh: 舊例，支使監諸廩出納，程訴於承業曰：「此事非仆所長，請擇能者。

translations.literal: By old custom the staff adjutant supervised all granary receipts and disbursements; Cheng complained to Chengye: "This matter is not what your servant excels at—please choose one who is capable."
translations.idiomatic: By custom the staff adjutant oversaw granary accounts; Cheng told Chengye, "This is not my strength—choose someone able."

sentences.zh: 」承業叱之曰：「公稱文士，即合飛文染翰，以濟霸國，嘗命草辭，自陳短拙，及留職務，又以為辭，公所能者何也？

translations.literal: " Chengye rebuked him: "You call yourself a man of letters—then you ought to fly with prose and stain the brush to aid the hegemonic state. Ordered once to draft a text, you declared yourself clumsy; when left with duties, you again make excuses—what, then, can you do?"
translations.idiomatic: " Chengye snapped, "You call yourself a scholar—then write for the cause! You pleaded incompetence when asked to draft, and now you shirk accounts—what can you do at all?"

sentences.zh: 」程垂泣謝之。

translations.literal: " Cheng wept and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng wept and apologized.

sentences.zh: 後曆觀察判官。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as adjutant to military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as adjutant on several circuits.

sentences.zh: 及汴將王彥章陷德勝南城，爭攻楊劉，莊宗禦軍苦戰，臣下憂之，鹹白宰臣，欲連章規諫，請不躬禦士伍。

translations.literal: When Bian general Wang Yanzhang took the southern city of Desheng and strove to attack Yangliu, Zhuangzong led the army in bitter fighting; his ministers were anxious and all told the chief ministers they wished to submit linked memorials remonstrating, asking that he not personally lead the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Yanzhang of Bian took southern Desheng and pressed Yangliu, Zhuangzong fought at the head of the army; alarmed ministers urged the chief councillors to petition jointly that he not expose himself in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革言及漢高臨廣武事，矢及於胸，紿雲中足。

translations.literal: Dou Luge spoke of Emperor Gaozu of Han at Guangwu, where an arrow reached his chest and he lied that it had struck his foot in the cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Luge cited how Gaozu of Han at Guangwu took an arrow in the chest yet claimed it had only grazed his foot.

sentences.zh: 程曰：「此劉季失策。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "That was Liu Ji's mistake in strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "That was Liu Bang's blunder."

sentences.zh: 」眾皆縮頸。

translations.literal: " All shrank their necks.
translations.idiomatic: " Everyone recoiled.

sentences.zh: 嘗論近世士族，或曰：「員外郎孔明龜，善和宰相之令緒，宣聖之係孫，得非盛歟！

translations.literal: Once, discussing recent eminent clans, someone said: "Vice Director Kongming Gui is skilled at harmonizing with the chief minister's orders, a collateral descendant of the Sage of Propagation—can this not be glorious!"
translations.idiomatic: Discussing recent great families, someone said, "Vice Director Kongming Gui can match a chief minister's command, and he is Confucius' descendant—is that not splendid!"

sentences.zh: 」程曰：「止於孔子之後，盛則吾不知也。

translations.literal: " Cheng said: "He stops at being after Confucius; as for glory, I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: " Cheng replied, "He is merely Confucius' descendant; as for glory, I see none."

sentences.zh: 」親黨有假驢夫於程者，程帖府給之，府吏訴雲無例，程怒鞭吏背。

translations.literal: " A kinsman asked Cheng to borrow a donkey driver; Cheng posted a note at the prefecture to supply one. The prefectural clerk complained there was no precedent; Cheng angrily whipped the clerk's back.
translations.idiomatic: " When a relative asked Cheng for a donkey driver, he ordered the prefecture to provide one; the clerk protested there was no precedent, and Cheng had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 時任圜為興唐少尹，莊宗從姊婿也，憑其寵戚，因詣程。

translations.literal: At the time Ren Huan was Junior Governor of Xingtang, Zhuangzong's cousin by marriage, relying on his favored kinship, and therefore came to see Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan was then Junior Governor of Xingtang, Zhuangzong's cousin-in-law, and came to Cheng relying on his court connections.

sentences.zh: 程方衣鶴氅、華陽巾，憑幾決事，見圜怒詈曰：「是何蟲豸，恃婦力耶！

translations.literal: Cheng was just then wearing a crane cloak and Huayang cap, leaning on a desk to decide affairs; seeing Huan he cursed in anger: "What kind of insect is this, relying on a woman's power!"
translations.idiomatic: Cheng sat in crane cloak and Huayang cap judging affairs at his desk; seeing Ren he raged, "What vermin is this, trading on his wife's family?"

sentences.zh: 宰相取給於府縣，得不識舊體！

translations.literal: A chief minister takes supplies from prefectures and counties—can he not recognize the old forms!
translations.idiomatic: A chief minister draws supplies from the prefectures—has he no sense of proper form!

sentences.zh: 」圜不言而退，是夜，馳至博平，麵訴於莊宗。

translations.literal: " Huan said nothing and withdrew; that night he galloped to Boping and complained in person to Zhuangzong.
translations.idiomatic: " Ren left without a word; that night he raced to Boping and told Zhuangzong face to face.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒，謂郭崇韜曰：「朕誤相此癡物，敢辱予九卿。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was angry and said to Guo Chongtao: "We wrongly made this fool a chief minister—he dares insult Our Nine Ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong fumed and told Guo Chongtao, "I was wrong to make this fool a minister—he dares insult my high officials."

sentences.zh: 」促令自盡。

translations.literal: " He urged that Cheng be made to take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered Cheng to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 崇韜亦怒，事幾不測，賴盧質橫身解之，遂降為右庶子。

translations.literal: Chongtao was also angry; the affair nearly became unpredictable, but thanks to Lu Zhi throwing himself across to mediate, Cheng was demoted to Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao was furious too and matters nearly spun out of control until Lu Zhi intervened bodily; Cheng was reduced to Right Subordinate of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 莊宗既定河南，程隨百官從幸洛陽，沿路墜馬，因病風而卒。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong secured Henan, Cheng followed the hundred officials in the imperial progress to Luoyang, fell from his horse along the road, and died of apoplexy.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong secured Henan, Cheng followed the court to Luoyang, fell from his horse on the road, and died of a stroke.

sentences.zh: 贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳，幽州人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng was a man of You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng was from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 少為儒。

translations.literal: In youth he was a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the classics in youth.

sentences.zh: 唐天祐中，燕帥劉守光盡率部內丁夫為軍伍，而黥其面，為儒者患之。

translations.literal: In Tang Tianyou, Yan commander Liu Shouguang conscripted all able-bodied men within his command as soldiers and tattooed their faces; scholars were distressed by this.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tang in Tianyou, Liu Shouguang of Yan drafted every able man as a soldier and branded their faces—a calamity for scholars.

sentences.zh: 多為僧以避之，鳳亦落發至太原。

translations.literal: Many became monks to avoid it; Feng also shaved his head and went to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Many took tonsure to escape; Feng shaved his head and fled to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 頃之，從劉守奇奔梁，梁用守奇為博州刺史，表鳳為判官。

translations.literal: Before long he followed Liu Shouqi in flight to Liang; Liang employed Shouqi as Prefect of Bo Prefecture and recommended Feng as adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he followed Liu Shouqi to Liang; Liang made Shouqi prefect of Bo and appointed Feng his adjutant.

sentences.zh: （案：下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: There is missing text below.))
translations.idiomatic: (Note: Text is missing below.))

sentences.zh: 為鄆州節度判官。

translations.literal: He served as adjutant to the military governor of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He became adjutant on the Yanzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗聞鳳名，得之甚喜，以為護鑾學士。

translations.literal: Tang's Zhuangzong heard Feng's name and was greatly pleased to obtain him, making him Guardian of the Imperial Carriage Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong heard of Feng and was delighted to have him, appointing him Guardian of the Imperial Carriage Academician.

sentences.zh: 後莊宗即位，拜鳳中書舍人。

translations.literal: Later, when Zhuangzong took the throne, Feng was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong ascended the throne, Feng was made Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 及入汴，改授禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When they entered Bian, he was reassigned as Vice Director in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: On entering Bian he was reassigned as Vice Director of Rites.

sentences.zh: 莊宗及劉皇后幸張全義第，後奏曰：「妾五六歲失父母，每見老者，思念尊親泣下，以全義年德，妾欲父事之，以慰孤女之心。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong and Empress Liu visited Zhang Quanyi's residence; the empress submitted: "Your servant lost her parents at five or six; whenever she sees the aged she weeps thinking of her elders. Because Quanyi is advanced in years, your servant wishes to treat him as a father to comfort an orphan's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong and Empress Liu visited Zhang Quanyi; the empress said, "I lost my parents at five or six; the sight of elders still moves me to tears. Quanyi is venerable in years—I wish to honor him as a father to comfort this orphan's heart."

sentences.zh: 」莊宗許之，命鳳作箋上全義，定往來儀注。

translations.literal: " Zhuangzong assented and ordered Feng to compose a letter to Quanyi and fix the ritual forms for their exchanges.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhuangzong agreed and told Feng to draft the letter to Quanyi and set the ceremonial forms between them.

sentences.zh: 鳳上書極諫，不納。

translations.literal: Feng submitted a memorial remonstrating to the utmost; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Feng memorialized in the strongest terms; the emperor would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 天成初，置端明殿學士，鳳與馮道俱任其職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tiancheng the Duanming Hall Academicians were established; Feng and Feng Dao both held the post.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tiancheng the Duanming Hall academicians were created; Feng and Feng Dao both served.

sentences.zh: 時任圜為宰相，為安重誨所傾，以至罷相歸磁州。

translations.literal: At the time Ren Huan was chief minister and was undermined by An Chonghui until he was removed from office and returned to Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan was then chief minister until An Chonghui brought him down and sent him home to Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 及朱守殷以汴州叛，馳驛賜圜自盡。

translations.literal: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bian Prefecture, a relay edict granted Ren death by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled at Bian, an express edict ordered Ren to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 既而鳳哭謂安重誨曰：「任圜，義士也，肯造逆謀以讎君父乎？

translations.literal: Then Feng wept and said to An Chonghui: "Ren Huan is a man of righteousness—would he contrive rebellion to avenge himself on ruler and father?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng then wept and told An Chonghui, "Ren Huan is an honorable man—would he plot rebellion against his sovereign?"

sentences.zh: 如此濫刑，何以安國！

translations.literal: With punishment so abused, how can the state be secured!
translations.idiomatic: How can the realm be secure when punishment is so abused!

sentences.zh: 」重誨笑而不責。

translations.literal: " Chonghui laughed and did not blame him.
translations.idiomatic: " Chonghui only smiled and did not reprove him.

sentences.zh: 是冬，權知貢舉。

translations.literal: That winter he acted as supervisor of the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he oversaw the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 明年春，有僧自西國取經回，得佛牙大如拳，褐漬皴裂，進於明宗。

translations.literal: The next spring a monk returned from the western lands with scriptures, obtaining a Buddha tooth as large as a fist, brown-stained and cracked, which he presented to Emperor Mingzong.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring a monk back from the west with scriptures presented Mingzong a Buddha tooth the size of a fist, stained brown and fissured.

sentences.zh: 鳳揚言曰：「 曾聞佛牙錘鍛不壞，請試之。

translations.literal: Feng proclaimed publicly: "I have heard that a Buddha tooth cannot be broken by hammering—let us test it."
translations.idiomatic: Feng declared aloud, "They say a Buddha tooth cannot be broken by hammering—let us try."

sentences.zh: 」隨斧而碎。

translations.literal: " It shattered at once under the axe.
translations.idiomatic: " It shattered at the first blow of the axe.

sentences.zh: 時宮中所施已逾數千緡，聞毀乃止。

translations.literal: By then the palace had already donated more than several thousand strings of cash; on hearing it was destroyed, the offerings stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The palace had already pledged thousands of strings of cash; when the relic was destroyed, the gifts ceased.

sentences.zh: 及車駕還洛，留知汴州事，尋授中書侍郎、平章事。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to Luo, he was left to manage Bian Prefecture affairs, soon appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: When the court returned to Luoyang he was left to govern Bian, then made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: （李之儀《姑溪居士集》：鳳為《莊宗實錄》，將何挺論劉煦疏不載，句既相，遂引鳳共政事。）〉

translations.literal: (Li Zhiyi's Guxi Jushi Collection: Feng compiled the Veritable Records of Zhuangzong; He Ting's discussion of Liu Xu's memorial was not included. Ju having become chief minister, he then brought Feng in to share government.))
translations.idiomatic: (Li Zhiyi's Guxi Jushi Collection notes that Feng compiled Zhuangzong's Veritable Records; He Ting's critique of Liu Xu's memorial went unpublished. When Ju became chief minister he brought Feng into government.))

sentences.zh: 長興中，安重誨出鎮河中，人無敢言者，惟鳳極言於上前曰：「重誨是陛下家臣，其心終不背主，五年秉權，賢豪俯伏，但不周防，自貽浸潤。

translations.literal: In Changxing, An Chonghui went out to govern Hezhong; no one dared speak, only Feng spoke to the utmost before the throne: "Chonghui is Your Majesty's household servant; his heart in the end will not turn against his lord. Five years holding power, the worthy and heroic bowed down—but through insufficient precaution he brought slander upon himself."
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing, when An Chonghui was sent to govern Hezhong, none dared speak except Feng, who told the throne, "Chonghui is your household servant and would never betray you. Five years in power bent every worthy to him—but by failing to guard himself he invited slander."

sentences.zh: 」明宗以為朋黨，不悅其奏。

translations.literal: " Mingzong took it as factionalism and was displeased with the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong saw factional motive in this and disliked the memorial.

sentences.zh: 重誨獲罪，乃出邢州節度使。

translations.literal: Chonghui was found guilty and was sent out as military governor of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghui fell, Feng was sent out as military governor of Xing.

sentences.zh: 及閔帝蒙塵於衛州，鳳集賓佐軍校，垂涕曰：「主上播遷，渡河而北，吾輩安坐不赴奔問，於禮可乎？

translations.literal: When Emperor Min suffered hardship at Wei Prefecture, Feng gathered guests, staff, and military officers and said with tears: "Our lord is cast adrift; he has crossed the river north—can we sit at ease and not rush to inquire after him—is that proper in ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min was driven into exile at Wei, Feng gathered his staff and officers in tears: "Our lord is adrift north of the river—can we sit idle and not go to him? Where is the duty in that?"

sentences.zh: 」軍校曰：「唯公所使。

translations.literal: " The military officers said: "We follow whatever you command."
translations.idiomatic: " The officers said, "We await your orders."

sentences.zh: 」將行，聞閔帝遇弑而止。

translations.literal: " Just as they were about to set out, they heard that Emperor Min had been assassinated and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " They were about to depart when news came that Emperor Min had been murdered, and they halted.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，召還，授太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai he was recalled and made Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai he was recalled and made Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 既而病足，不能朝謁。

translations.literal: Soon afterward his feet were afflicted and he could not attend court audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his feet failed him and he could no longer attend court.

sentences.zh: 疾篤，自為蓍筮，卦成，投蓍而歎曰：「吾家世無五十者，而復窮賤；

translations.literal: When his illness was grave he divined for himself with yarrow stalks; when the hexagram was complete he cast the stalks aside and sighed: "In my family for generations none has reached fifty, and again been poor and lowly;
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened he cast the yarrow stalks himself; when the hexagram was done he threw them down and sighed, "No man in my line has ever lived past fifty, and we have always been poor;

sentences.zh: 吾年已五十，又為將相，豈有遐壽哉！

translations.literal: I am already fifty and have also been general and minister—how could there be long life!"
translations.idiomatic: I am fifty and have been general and minister—how could I hope for long life!"

sentences.zh: 」清泰二年三月卒。

translations.literal: " He died in the third month of the second year of Qingtai.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in the third month of Qingtai 2.

sentences.zh: 鳳性豁達，輕財重義，凡士友以窮厄告者，必傾其資而餉之，人士以此多之也。

translations.literal: Feng's nature was open and generous; he prized righteousness over wealth. Whenever scholar-friends reported distress, he would pour out his resources to support them—men of the world therefore praised him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Feng was open-handed and valued honor over wealth; any scholar-friend in need received all he could give, and for this men esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 李愚，字子晦。

translations.literal: Li Yu, style Zihui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, styled Zihui.

sentences.zh: 自稱趙郡平棘西祖之後，家世為儒。

translations.literal: He claimed descent from the western ancestor of Pingji in Zhao Commandery; his family for generations were Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: He claimed descent from the Pingji line in Zhao; his family had been scholars for generations.

sentences.zh: 父瞻業，應進士不第，遇亂，徙家渤海之無棣，以詩書訓子孫。

translations.literal: His father Zhanye sat for the jinshi but did not pass; encountering turmoil, he moved the family to Wudi in Bohai and taught his descendants with poetry and books.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhanye failed the jinshi examination; in the chaos he moved the family to Wudi on the Bohai coast and raised his children on the classics.

sentences.zh: 愚童齔時，謹重有異常兒，年長方誌學，遍閱經史。

translations.literal: In childhood Yu was grave beyond ordinary boys; only when grown did he set his will on learning, reading widely in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: As a child Yu was unusually solemn; only in maturity did he devote himself to learning and read widely in the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 慕晏嬰之為人，初名晏平。

translations.literal: He admired Yan Ying's character and was at first named Yanping.
translations.idiomatic: Admiring Yan Ying, he was first named Yanping.

sentences.zh: 為文尚氣格，有韓、柳體。

translations.literal: In writing he prized vigor of style, with the manner of Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His prose favored force and structure in the manner of Han Yu and Liu Zongyuan.

sentences.zh: 厲誌端莊，風神峻整，非禮不言，行不苟且。

translations.literal: He disciplined his will to be dignified and upright, his bearing stern and ordered; he spoke nothing outside ritual and acted without carelessness.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated a grave, upright bearing, spoke only as propriety allowed, and never acted carelessly.

sentences.zh: 愚初以艱貧，求為假官，滄州盧彥威署安陵簿。

translations.literal: Yu at first, because of hardship and poverty, sought a provisional post; Lu Yanwei of Cang Prefecture appointed him registrar of Anling.
translations.idiomatic: Poor at the outset, Yu sought a temporary post and Lu Yanwei of Cangzhou made him registrar of Anling.

sentences.zh: 丁憂，服闋，隨計之長安。

translations.literal: He observed mourning; when the mourning period ended he went with the examination cohort to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning ended he traveled to Chang'an for the examinations.

sentences.zh: 屬關輔亂離，頻年罷舉，客於蒲、華之間。

translations.literal: As the Guanzhong region was in turmoil and separation, examinations were suspended for years; he sojourned between Pu and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: With Guanzhong in chaos the examinations were suspended for years, and he lived as a guest between Pu and Hua.

sentences.zh: 光化中，軍容劉季述、王奉先廢昭宗，立裕王，五月餘，諸侯無奔問者。

translations.literal: In Guanghua, Army Commissioner Liu Jishu and Wang Fengxian deposed Emperor Zhaozong and enthroned Prince Yu; for more than five months no regional lord came to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In Guanghua, Liu Jishu and Wang Fengxian deposed Zhaozong and set up Prince Yu; for five months no prince came to the emperor's aid.

sentences.zh: 愚時在華陰，致書於華帥韓建，其略曰：「仆關東一布衣耳，幸讀書為文，每見君臣父子之際，有傷教害義之事，常痛心切齒，恨不得抽腸蹀血，肆之市朝。

translations.literal: Yu was then at Huayin and sent a letter to Hua commander Han Jian, in summary saying: "Your servant is but a plain-clothed man of the eastern passes, fortunate to read books and write. Whenever I see between ruler and minister, father and son, matters that wound teaching and harm righteousness, I constantly ache to the marrow and grind my teeth, wishing I could tear out my entrails and trample blood, exposing it in the market and court."
translations.idiomatic: Yu was then at Huayin and wrote to Han Jian, commander of Hua, in essence: "I am only a commoner of the east who has been blessed to read and write. Whenever I see what wounds the bonds of ruler and subject, father and son, I ache with rage and would gladly tear out my own entrails and trample them in the public square."

sentences.zh: 明公居近關重鎮，君父幽辱月餘，坐視凶逆，而忘勤王之舉，仆所未喻也。

translations.literal: Your Excellency holds a key post near the passes; ruler and father have suffered disgrace for more than a month, yet you sit and watch the vicious rebels and forget the effort to rescue the throne—this your servant cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: You hold a strategic post at the passes, yet for more than a month you have watched your sovereign humiliated and done nothing to rescue the throne—I cannot fathom it.

sentences.zh: 仆竊計中朝輔弼，雖有誌而無權；

translations.literal: Your servant privately considers that the central court's assistants, though they have will, lack power;
translations.idiomatic: The ministers at court may have the will but lack the power;

sentences.zh: 外鎮諸侯，雖有權而無誌。

translations.literal: the frontier lords, though they have power, lack will.
translations.idiomatic: the regional lords have power but lack the will.

sentences.zh: 惟明公忠義，社稷是依。

translations.literal: Only Your Excellency is loyal and righteous—the altars of state depend on you.
translations.idiomatic: Only you are loyal and righteous—the realm depends on you.

sentences.zh: 往年車輅播遷，號泣奉迎，累歲供饋，再復朝廟，義感人心，至今歌詠。

translations.literal: In former years when the imperial carriage was cast adrift, you wept and welcomed it; for years you supplied provisions and restored the court to the ancestral temple—righteousness moved men's hearts and is sung to this day.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne was driven into exile before, you wept as you welcomed the emperor back, fed the court for years, and restored the ancestral rites—men still sing of that loyalty.

sentences.zh: 此時事勢，尤異於前，明公地處要衝，位兼將相，自宮闈變故，已涉旬時，若不號令率先，以圖反正，遲疑未決，一朝山東侯伯唱義連衡，鼓行而西，明公求欲自安，如何決策！

translations.literal: The situation at this time is especially different from before. Your Excellency stands at a strategic choke point, your post combining general and minister. Since the palace upheaval, more than ten days have passed; if you do not take the lead with proclamations to restore the proper order, hesitating undecided, then one morning the lords of Shandong may raise righteousness in alliance, beat drums and march west—how will Your Excellency seek your own safety, how decide!
translations.idiomatic: Matters are worse now. You stand at the vital pass with both civil and military authority; the palace coup is already ten days old. If you do not lead the call to restore the throne, and eastern lords unite and march west with drums beating—how will you keep yourself safe then!

sentences.zh: 此必然之勢也。

translations.literal: This is the inevitable trend.
translations.idiomatic: That is the inevitable course of events.

sentences.zh: 不如馳檄四方，諭以逆順，軍聲一振，則元凶破膽，浹旬之間，二豎之首傳於天下，計無便於此者。

translations.literal: Better to dispatch proclamations swiftly to the four quarters, instructing them in treason and loyalty; once army renown shakes, the chief villains will lose heart, and within ten days the heads of the two petty fellows will be announced throughout the realm—no plan is more advantageous than this.
translations.idiomatic: Better to send swift proclamations across the realm teaching loyalty and treason; once your armies stir, the chief culprits will lose heart, and within ten days the heads of those two wretches will be announced to the empire—no wiser course exists.

sentences.zh: 」建深禮遇之，堅辭還山。

translations.literal: " Jian treated him with deep courtesy, but Yu firmly declined and returned to the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian honored him deeply, but Yu firmly refused and returned to seclusion.

sentences.zh: 天復初，駕在鳳翔，汴軍攻蒲、華，愚避難東歸洛陽。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu the imperial carriage was at Fengxiang; Bian armies attacked Pu and Hua; Yu fled east and returned to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu, with the court at Fengxiang and Bian armies attacking Pu and Hua, Yu fled east to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 時衛公李德裕孫延古在平泉舊墅，愚往依焉。

translations.literal: At the time Duke Wei Li Deyu's grandson Yangu was at the old villa at Pingquan; Yu went to rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu's grandson Yangu was then at the old Pingquan estate, and Yu went to live with him.

sentences.zh: 子弟親采梠負薪，以給朝夕，未嘗幹人。

translations.literal: He and the younger men personally gathered mulberry leaves and carried firewood to supply day and night, never importuning others.
translations.idiomatic: He and his kin gathered mulberry leaves and firewood themselves for their daily needs and never importuned others.

sentences.zh: 故少師薛廷珪掌貢籍之歲，登進士第；

translations.literal: In the year when former Junior Mentor Xue Tinggui managed the examination registers, he passed the jinshi;
translations.idiomatic: In the year Xue Tinggui oversaw the examination registers he passed the jinshi;

sentences.zh: 又登宏詞料，授河南府參軍，遂下居洛表白沙之別墅。

translations.literal: he also passed the Hongci examination and was appointed Army Adjutant of Henan Prefecture, then went down to dwell at a villa at Baisha on the Luo plateau.
translations.idiomatic: he also passed the Hongci examination, became adjutant of Henan, and settled at a villa at Baisha on the Luoyang plateau.

sentences.zh: 梁有禪代之謀，柳璨希旨殺害朝士，愚以衣冠自相殘害，乃避地河朔，與宗人李延光客於山東。

translations.literal: Liang had designs for usurping the mandate; Liu Can to curry favor killed court gentlemen; Yu, seeing the gentry destroy one another, fled to the north of the Yellow River and with his clansman Li Yangu sojourned as guests in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang plotted to seize the throne and Liu Can slaughtered courtiers to please his masters, Yu fled to Hebei and lodged in Shandong with his kinsman Li Yangu.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝嗣位，雅好儒士，延光素相款奉，得侍講禁中，屢言愚之行高學贍，有史魚、蘧瑗之風。

translations.literal: Liang's Last Emperor succeeded; he elegantly loved Confucian scholars. Yangu had long been cordial with him and obtained a lecturing post within the palace, repeatedly saying Yu's conduct was lofty and learning ample, with the air of Shiyu and Qu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang's Last Emperor succeeded he favored scholars; Yangu, long his companion in the inner palace, often praised Yu's integrity and learning as rivaling the ancients Shiyu and Qu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 召見，嗟賞久之，擢為左拾遺。

translations.literal: Summoned to audience, the emperor sighed in admiration for a long while and promoted him to Left Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: Called to audience, the emperor admired him at length and made him Left Remonstrance Official.

sentences.zh: 俄充崇政院直學士，或預谘謀，而儼然正色，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Soon he served as Direct Academician of the Chongzheng Hall, sometimes taking part in counsel, yet stern in countenance, not fearing the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was Direct Academician of the Chongzheng Hall; though he sometimes advised on policy, he remained stern and unafraid of the powerful.

sentences.zh: 衡王入朝，重臣李振輩皆致拜，惟愚長揖。

translations.literal: Prince Heng entered court; heavy ministers such as Li Zhen all performed full bows, only Yu gave a long clasped-hand salute.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Heng attended court, grandees like Li Zhen all bowed low; only Yu gave a formal clasped-hand salute.

sentences.zh: 末帝讓之曰：「衡王，朕之兄。

translations.literal: The Last Emperor reproved him: "Prince Heng is Our elder brother."
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor reproved him: "Prince Heng is my elder brother."

sentences.zh: 朕猶致拜，崇政使李振等皆拜，爾何傲耶！

translations.literal: We still perform full bows; Chongzheng Commissioner Li Zhen and the rest all bow—why are you so arrogant!"
translations.idiomatic: I still bow to him, and Li Zhen and the rest all bow—why are you so arrogant!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下以家人禮兄，振等私臣也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your Majesty treats your brother with family rites; Zhen and the rest are private retainers."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Your Majesty honors him as family; Zhen and the others are your private servants."

sentences.zh: 臣居朝列，與王無素，安敢諂事。

translations.literal: Your servant stands in the court ranks and has no prior acquaintance with the prince—how would I dare fawn upon him?
translations.idiomatic: I stand in the court ranks and am no acquaintance of the prince—how should I fawn on him?

sentences.zh: 」其剛毅如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his firmness.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was his firmness.

sentences.zh: 晉州節度使華溫琪在任違法，籍民家財，其家訟於朝，製使劾之，伏罪。

translations.literal: Jin Prefecture Military Governor Hua Wenqi while in office violated the law, registering common people's family wealth; the family sued at court, and an imperial commissioner investigated him; he confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Wenqi, military governor of Jinzhou, seized commoners' property in violation of law; the families sued at court, an imperial commissioner investigated, and he confessed.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝以先朝草昧之臣，不忍加法，愚堅按其罪。

translations.literal: Liang's Last Emperor, because he was a minister from the founding days of the former court, was unwilling to apply the law; Yu firmly pressed his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor, treating him as a founding-era minister, was reluctant to punish him; Yu insisted on pressing the charge.

sentences.zh: 梁末帝詔曰：「朕若不與鞫窮，謂予不念赤子；

translations.literal: Liang's Last Emperor issued an edict: "If We do not investigate to the end, it will be said We do not care for the common people;
translations.idiomatic: The Last Emperor decreed: "If I do not investigate thoroughly, men will say I do not care for the people;

sentences.zh: 若或遂行典憲，謂予不念功臣。

translations.literal: if We then carry out the statutes and ordinances, it will be said We do not care for meritorious ministers."
translations.idiomatic: if I then execute the law, men will say I do not care for meritorious servants."

sentences.zh: 為爾君者，不亦難乎！

translations.literal: To be your ruler—is it not also difficult!
translations.idiomatic: To be your ruler—is that not hard!

sentences.zh: 其華溫琪所受贓，宜官給代還所訟之家。

translations.literal: As for the bribes Hua Wenqi received, the government should supply funds to repay the families who sued.
translations.idiomatic: The bribes Hua Wenqi took shall be repaid to the suing families from public funds.

sentences.zh: 」貞明中，通事舍人李霄傭夫毆僦舍人致死，法司案律，罪在李霄。

translations.literal: " In Zhenming, Courier Gentleman Li Xiao's hired laborer beat a tenant to death; the judicial office applied the statutes, placing guilt on Li Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: " In Zhenming, Li Xiao's hired man beat a tenant to death; the judicial office found Li Xiao guilty under the law.

sentences.zh: 愚白：「李霄手不鬥毆。

translations.literal: Yu stated: "Li Xiao's own hands did not fight or beat."
translations.idiomatic: Yu argued, "Li Xiao did not strike the blow himself."

sentences.zh: 庸夫致死，安得坐其主耶！

translations.literal: A common fellow caused death—how can his master be made to bear guilt!
translations.idiomatic: A hired man killed someone—how can his master be punished for it!

sentences.zh: 」以是忤旨。

translations.literal: " By this he offended the imperial will.
translations.idiomatic: " This defied the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 愚自拾遺再遷膳部員外郎，賜緋，改司勳員外郎，賜紫，至是罷職，曆許、鄧觀察判官。

translations.literal: Yu from Remonstrance Official was again promoted to Vice Director of Provisions, granted scarlet; changed to Vice Director of Merit, granted purple; at this point he was removed from office and successively served as adjutant on the Xu and Deng observation circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yu rose from Remonstrance Official to Vice Director of Provisions with scarlet robes, then Vice Director of Merit with purple; after this setback he served as adjutant on the Xu and Deng circuits.

sentences.zh: 初在內職，慈州舉子張礪依焉。

translations.literal: When he was first in inner service, Cizhou examination candidate Zhang Li relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: While he held inner-court posts, the Cizhou candidate Zhang Li attached himself to him.

sentences.zh: 貞明中，礪自河陽北歸莊宗，補授太原府掾，出入崇闥之間，揄揚愚之節概，及言愚之所為文《仲尼遇》、《顏回壽》、《夷齊非餓人》等篇，北人望風稱之。

translations.literal: In Zhenming, Li returned north from Heyang to Zhuangzong, was appointed supplementarily as an aide of Taiyuan Prefecture, and going in and out among the lofty gates praised Yu's integrity and conduct, also speaking of Yu's writings such as "Confucius Encountered," "Yan Hui's Longevity," and "Boyi and Shuqi Were Not Starving Men"; northerners at the wind's report praised him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming, Li went north from Heyang to Zhuangzong, became an aide in Taiyuan, and moving among the court gates praised Yu's integrity and cited his essays "Confucius Encountered," "Yan Hui's Longevity," and "Boyi and Shuqi Were Not Starving Men"—northerners praised Yu at once.

sentences.zh: 洎莊宗都洛陽，鄧帥俾奏章入朝，諸貴見之，禮接如舊。

translations.literal: By the time Zhuangzong made Luoyang his capital, the Deng commander had him submit a memorial to court; the various nobles on seeing him received him with ceremony as of old.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong established his capital at Luoyang, the Deng commander sent Yu to court; the great men received him with their former courtesy.

sentences.zh: 尋為主客郎中，數月，召為翰林學士。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Director of the Host and Guest Bureau; after several months he was summoned as Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became Director of the Host and Guest Bureau, and within months was summoned to the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 三年，魏王繼岌征蜀，請為都統判官，仍帶本職從軍。

translations.literal: In the third year, when Prince of Wei Jiji campaigned against Shu, Yu requested to be adjutant to the commander-in-chief, still bearing his original post as he followed the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Prince Jiji campaigned against Shu, Yu asked to serve as the commander's adjutant while keeping his existing post in the field.

sentences.zh: 時物議以蜀險阻，未可長驅，郭崇韜問計於愚，愚曰：「如聞蜀人厭其主荒恣，倉卒必不為用。

translations.literal: At the time public opinion held that Shu was perilous and obstructed, not fit for a long drive; Guo Chongtao asked Yu for a plan. Yu said: "As I hear, the people of Shu detest their ruler's wasteful license; in haste he surely will not be used."
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion held that Shu's terrain forbade a long advance; when Guo Chongtao asked Yu's counsel, Yu said, "The Shu people despise their ruler's excesses—they will not stand by him in a crisis."

sentences.zh: 宜乘其人二三，風馳電擊，彼必破膽，安能守險。

translations.literal: We ought to seize the moment when men are but two or three parts loyal, strike like wind and lightning—they will surely lose heart; how could they hold the passes?
translations.idiomatic: Strike while their loyalty is divided, move like wind and lightning, and they will lose heart—how could they hold the passes?

sentences.zh: 」及前軍至固鎮，收軍食十五萬斛，崇韜喜，謂愚曰：「公能料事，吾軍濟矣！

translations.literal: " When the vanguard reached Guzhen and collected one hundred fifty thousand hu of army grain, Chongtao rejoiced and said to Yu: "You can foresee events—our army is saved!"
translations.idiomatic: " When the vanguard reached Guzhen and gathered 150,000 hu of grain, Chongtao rejoiced and told Yu, "You foresaw this—our army is saved!"

sentences.zh: 」招討判官陳乂至寶雞，稱疾乞留在後。

translations.literal: " Pacification adjutant Chen Yi reached Baoji and claimed illness, begging to remain in the rear.
translations.idiomatic: " Pacification adjutant Chen Yi reached Baoji and pleaded illness to stay behind.

sentences.zh: 愚厲聲曰：「陳乂見利則進，懼難則止。

translations.literal: Yu said in a harsh voice: "Chen Yi advances when he sees profit and stops when he fears hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Yu said sharply, "Chen Yi advances when he sees gain and halts when he fears danger."

sentences.zh: 今大軍涉險，人心易惑，正可斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Now the great army crosses peril; men's hearts are easily unsettled—this is exactly when he should be beheaded to warn the host.
translations.idiomatic: The army is in peril and morale is fragile—he should be executed as an example.

sentences.zh: 」由是軍人無遲留者。

translations.literal: " From this, no soldier in the army lingered.
translations.idiomatic: " After that no soldier dared linger.

sentences.zh: 是時，軍書羽檄，皆出其手。

translations.literal: At this time military documents and urgent dispatches all came from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: At that time all military orders and urgent dispatches came from his pen.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，就拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was immediately appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu fell he was appointed Secretariat Drafter on the spot.

sentences.zh: 師還，明宗即位。

translations.literal: The army returned; Mingzong took the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The army returned as Mingzong ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 時西征副招討使任圜為宰相，雅相欽重，屢言於安重誨，請引為同列；

translations.literal: At the time Western Campaign Deputy Pacification Commissioner Ren Huan was chief minister and elegantly esteemed Yu, repeatedly speaking to An Chonghui to bring him into the same rank;
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan, then chief minister and former deputy commander of the western campaign, greatly admired Yu and repeatedly asked An Chonghui to make him a fellow councillor;

sentences.zh: 屬孔循用事，援引崔協以塞其請。

translations.literal: but as Kong Xun held power, he brought in Cui Xie to block the request.
translations.idiomatic: but Kong Xun was in power and installed Cui Xie to block the appointment.

sentences.zh: 俄以本職權知貢舉，改兵部侍郎，充翰林承旨。

translations.literal: Soon, in his original post he acted as supervisor of examinations, was changed to Vice Minister of War, and served as Hanlin Academician-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he oversaw the examinations in his existing post, became Vice Minister of War, and served as Chief Hanlin Academician.

sentences.zh: 長興初，除太常卿，屬趙鳳出鎮邢台，乃拜中書侍郎、平章事，轉集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changxing he was made Minister of Ceremonies; as Zhao Feng went out to govern Xingtai, Yu was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor, then transferred to Grand Academician of the Jixian Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Changxing he became Minister of Ceremonies; when Zhao Feng left for Xingtai, Yu was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor, then Grand Academician of Jixian.

sentences.zh: 長興季年，秦王恣橫，權要之臣，避禍不暇，邦之存亡，無敢言者。

translations.literal: In the late years of Changxing the Prince of Qin acted with reckless license; powerful ministers had no leisure to avoid calamity; on the state's survival or destruction, none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Changxing the Prince of Qin ran riot; powerful ministers scrambled to avoid disaster, and none dared speak of the realm's survival.

sentences.zh: 愚性剛介，往往形言，然人無唱和者。

translations.literal: Yu by nature was firm and upright and often gave voice to his views, yet no one echoed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was upright and outspoken, yet no one joined him.

sentences.zh: 後轉門下侍郎，監修國史，兼吏部尚書，與諸儒修成《創業功臣傳》三十卷。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Vice Director of the Chancellery, supervised compilation of the national history, and concurrently served as Minister of Personnel; with various scholars he completed the thirty-juan Biographies of Founding Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Vice Director of the Chancellery, oversaw the national history, and concurrently headed Personnel; with other scholars he completed the thirty-juan Biographies of Founding Merit.

sentences.zh: 愚初不治第，既命為相，官借延賓館居之。

translations.literal: Yu at first did not build a mansion; once appointed chief minister, the government lent him the Guest Reception Lodge to dwell in.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had never built a mansion; once made chief minister he lived in the government guest lodge.

sentences.zh: 嘗有疾，詔近臣宣諭，延之中堂，設席惟筦秸，使人言之，明宗特賜帷帳茵褥。

translations.literal: Once when he was ill, an edict sent a nearby minister to convey inquiries; received in the central hall, the seat set out was only bamboo and straw; the envoy reported this, and Mingzong specially granted curtains, canopies, and bedding.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill the emperor sent a courtier to inquire after him; in the central hall Yu offered only a mat of bamboo and straw; when the envoy reported this, Mingzong specially sent curtains and bedding.

sentences.zh: （《職官分紀》云：長興四年，愚病，明宗遣中使宣問。

translations.literal: (Records of Official Posts states: In the fourth year of Changxing, Yu was ill; Mingzong sent a palace envoy to convey inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: (Records of Official Posts notes: In Changxing 4 Yu fell ill and Mingzong sent a palace envoy to inquire.

sentences.zh: 愚所居寢室，蕭然四壁，病榻弊氈而已。

translations.literal: Yu's sleeping chamber was bare on all four walls, with only a worn rug on the sick couch.
translations.idiomatic: His bedchamber was bare on every side, with only a worn rug on his sickbed.

sentences.zh: 中使具言其事，帝曰：「宰相月俸幾何？

translations.literal: The envoy reported the matter in full; the emperor said: "How much is a chief minister's monthly salary?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported everything; the emperor said, "How much is a chief minister's monthly salary?"

sentences.zh: 而委頓如此。

translations.literal: Yet he is so worn down as this."
translations.idiomatic: And he is reduced to this."

sentences.zh: 」詔賜絹百匹、錢百千、帷帳什物一十三事。）〉

translations.literal: " An edict granted one hundred bolts of silk, a hundred thousand in cash, and thirteen items of curtains, canopies, and miscellaneous goods.))
translations.idiomatic: " He decreed a gift of one hundred bolts of silk, a hundred thousand cash, and thirteen sets of curtains and furnishings.))

sentences.zh: 閔帝嗣位，誌修德政，易月之制才除，便延訪學士讀《貞觀政要》、《太宗實錄》，有意於致理。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min succeeded, he resolved to cultivate virtuous government; the one-year mourning period had just ended when he summoned academicians to read Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign and Veritable Records of Emperor Taizong, intending to bring order.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min succeeded he vowed good government; scarcely had mourning ended when he summoned scholars to read Essentials of Zhenguan Governance and Taizong's Veritable Records, intent on good rule.

sentences.zh: 愚私謂同列曰：「吾君延訪，少及吾輩，位高責重，事亦堪憂，奈宗社何！

translations.literal: Yu privately told his colleagues: "Our lord's extended inquiries scarcely reach us; our posts are high and responsibility heavy—the matter is also worrisome; what of the altars of state!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu told his colleagues privately, "The emperor's consultations barely reach us, yet we bear heavy responsibility—what will become of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 」皆惕息而不敢言。

translations.literal: " All held their breath in fear and did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: " All held their breath and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 以恩例進位左僕射。

translations.literal: By favor he was advanced to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By grace of office he was promoted to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，徽陵禮畢，馮道出鎮同州，愚加特進、太微宮使、宏文館大學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, when the Huiling rites were complete and Feng Dao went out to govern Tong Prefecture, Yu was given special advancement, made Commissioner of the Taiwei Palace, and Grand Academician of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai, after the imperial tomb rites and Feng Dao's departure for Tongzhou, Yu received special advancement and became Commissioner of the Taiwei Palace and Grand Academician of Hongwen.

sentences.zh: 宰相劉句與馮道為婚家，道既出鎮，兩人在中書，或舊事不便要厘革者，對論不定。

translations.literal: Chief minister Liu Gou and Feng Dao were related by marriage; once Dao had gone out to his command, the two men were in the Secretariat, and on old matters that were inconvenient to reform or clarify, their face-to-face debates could not be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Liu Gou was related to Feng Dao by marriage; with Dao gone, he and Yu sat in the Secretariat and argued endlessly over old policies neither wished to change.

sentences.zh: 愚性太峻，因曰：「此事賢家翁所為，更之不亦便乎！
