translations.literal: Yu's nature was too stern; he therefore said: "This matter was done by your worthy father-in-law—would it not be convenient to change it!"
translations.idiomatic: Yu was too blunt and said, "Your father-in-law arranged this—wouldn't it be easier to change it!"

sentences.zh: 」句憾其言切，於是每言必相折難，或至喧呼。

translations.literal: " Gou resented his cutting words; from then on every remark became mutual refutation and difficulty, sometimes reaching shouting.
translations.idiomatic: " Gou resented the barb; thereafter every discussion turned into dispute, sometimes shouting.

sentences.zh: 無幾，兩人俱罷相守本官。

translations.literal: Before long, both men were removed from office and kept their original posts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon both were dismissed as chief ministers but kept their original ranks.

sentences.zh: 清泰二年秋，愚已嬰疾，率多請告，累表乞骸，不允，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year of Qingtai, Yu was already gravely ill, frequently requesting leave, repeatedly memorializing to beg his bones; it was not granted, and he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Qingtai 2 Yu was gravely ill, repeatedly asked leave and begged to retire; refused, he died in office.

sentences.zh: 任圜，京兆三原人。

translations.literal: Ren Huan was a man of Sanyuan in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan was from Sanyuan in the capital district.

sentences.zh: 祖清，成都少尹。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qing was Junior Governor of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qing had been Junior Governor of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 父茂宏，避地太原，奏授西河令；

translations.literal: His father Maohong fled to Taiyuan and was memorialized into appointment as magistrate of Xihe;
translations.idiomatic: His father Maohong fled to Taiyuan and was appointed magistrate of Xihe;

sentences.zh: 有子五人，曰圖、回、圜、團、冏，風彩俱異。

translations.literal: he had five sons named Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong, each with a distinct bearing.
translations.idiomatic: and had five sons—Tu, Hui, Huan, Tuan, and Jiong—each striking in his own way.

sentences.zh: 武皇愛之，以宗女妻團，歷代、憲二郡刺史。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor favored him, gave an imperial clanswoman in marriage to Tuan, and he served successively as prefect of Dai and Xian commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor favored the family, married a clanswoman to Tuan, and he served as prefect of Dai and Xian.

sentences.zh: 李嗣昭典兵於晉陽，與圜遊處甚洽，及鎮澤潞，請為觀察支使，解褐，賜朱紱。

translations.literal: Li Sizhao commanded armies at Jinyang and was on very friendly terms with Huan in travel and residence; when he governed Ze and Lu, he requested Huan as observation adjutant; he doffed commoner's dress and was granted the scarlet sash.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao commanded at Jinyang and was close to Huan; when he governed Ze-Lu he made Huan his adjutant, and Huan entered official life with the scarlet sash.

sentences.zh: 圜美姿容，有口辯。

translations.literal: Huan had handsome features and eloquence in debate.
translations.idiomatic: Huan was handsome and eloquent.

sentences.zh: 嗣昭為人間諜於莊宗，方有微隙，圜奉使往來，常申理之，克成友於之道，圜之力也。

translations.literal: Sizhao sent men to spy on Zhuangzong; there was then a slight rift; Huan went back and forth on missions and often explained and set things right, achieving the way of brotherly friendship—this was Huan's power.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhao had spies watching Zhuangzong and a rift had opened; Huan shuttled between them, reconciled them, and restored their brotherly bond—his doing.

sentences.zh: 及丁母憂，莊宗承製起復潞州觀察判官，賜紫。

translations.literal: When he completed mourning for his mother, Zhuangzong by imperial order recalled him to service as adjutant on the Lu observation circuit and granted purple.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's mourning Zhuangzong recalled him to adjutant on the Lu circuit and granted purple robes.

sentences.zh: 常山之役，嗣昭為帥，卒於軍，圜代總其事，號令如一，敵人不知。

translations.literal: In the campaign at Changshan, Sizhao was commander and died in the army; Huan took over command of affairs, orders as one, and the enemy did not know.
translations.idiomatic: At Changshan Sizhao commanded and died in battle; Huan took command seamlessly so the enemy never knew.

sentences.zh: 莊宗聞之，倍加獎賞。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong heard of it and doubled his rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong heard and rewarded him doubly.

sentences.zh: 是秋，復以上黨之師攻常山，城中萬人突出，大將孫文進死之，賊逼我軍，圜麾騎士擊之，頗有殺獲。

translations.literal: That autumn, again with the Shangdang army he attacked Changshan; ten thousand men in the city burst out, and great general Sun Wenjin was killed; the rebels pressed our army; Huan commanded the horsemen to strike them and had considerable kills and captures.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he again attacked Changshan with the Shangdang army; ten thousand defenders sallied forth and killed General Sun Wenjin; Huan led the cavalry counterattack with heavy kills.

sentences.zh: 嘗以禍福諭其城中，鎮人信之，使乞降。

translations.literal: He once instructed the city on fortune and calamity; the garrison men believed him and were made to beg surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He preached fortune and ruin to the city; the garrison believed him and sued for surrender.

sentences.zh: 及城潰，誅元惡之外，官吏鹹保其家屬，亦圜所庇護焉。

translations.literal: When the city collapsed, beyond executing the chief villains, officials and clerks all preserved their families—this too was under Huan's protection.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, beyond executing the ringleaders, he spared officials and their families—Huan's protection.

sentences.zh: 莊宗改鎮州為北京，以圜為工部尚書兼真定尹、北京副留守，行留守事。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong changed Zhen Prefecture to Northern Capital; he made Huan Minister of Works and concurrently Governor of Zhending and Deputy Northern Capital Rear-President, acting rear-presidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong made Zhenzhou the Northern Capital and appointed Huan Minister of Works, Governor of Zhending, and acting deputy rear-president of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 明年，郭崇韜兼鎮，改行軍司馬，充北面水陸轉運使，仍知府事。

translations.literal: The next year, when Guo Chongtao also held the command, Huan was changed to army march secretary, made Northern Front land-and-water transport commissioner, and still managed prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, under Guo Chongtao's joint command, he became army secretary and Northern Front transport commissioner while still governing the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，歸朝，守工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he returned to court and held the post of Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 3 he returned to court as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 崇韜伐蜀，奏令從征，西蜀平，署圜黔南節度使，懇辭遂止。

translations.literal: Chongtao campaigned against Shu and memorialized that Huan follow the expedition; when Western Shu was pacified, he appointed Huan military governor of Qiannan; Huan earnestly declined and it was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao campaigned against Shu, Huan accompanied him; after Shu fell he was offered Qiannan but earnestly declined.

sentences.zh: 魏王班師，行及利州，康延孝叛，以勁兵八千回劫西川。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei withdrew the army; when they reached Li Prefecture, Kang Yanxiao rebelled and with eight thousand crack troops turned back to raid Western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: As the prince withdrew, reaching Lizhou, Kang Yanxiao rebelled with eight thousand elite troops and raided Shu.

sentences.zh: 繼岌聞之，夜半命中使李廷安召圜，圜方寢，廷安登其床以告之，圜衣不及帶，遽見繼岌。

translations.literal: Jiji heard of it; at midnight he ordered palace envoy Li Ting'an to summon Huan. Huan was just asleep; Ting'an climbed onto his bed to tell him; Huan had no time to belt his robe and hurried to see Jiji.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji heard at midnight and sent Li Ting'an to summon Huan from his bed; Huan rushed to him without belting his robe.

sentences.zh: 繼岌泣而言曰：「紹琛負恩，非尚書不能制。

translations.literal: Jiji wept and said: "Shaochen has betrayed grace—only the Vice Director can control him."
translations.idiomatic: Jiji wept and said, "Shaochen has turned traitor—only you can stop him."

sentences.zh: 」即署圜為招討副使，與都指揮使梁漢顒等率兵攻延孝於漢州，擒之。

translations.literal: " He immediately appointed Huan deputy pacification commissioner; with Commander-in-Chief Liang Hanyong and others he led troops to attack Yanxiao at Han Prefecture and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: " He made Huan deputy pacification commissioner; with Liang Hanyong and others he attacked Yanxiao at Hanzhou and captured him.

sentences.zh: 旋至渭南，繼岌遇害。

translations.literal: Soon they reached Weinan; Jiji was murdered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, at Weinan, Jiji was murdered.

sentences.zh: 圜代總全師，朝於洛陽。

translations.literal: Huan took over command of the entire army and presented himself at court in Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Huan took command of the whole army and presented himself at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 明宗嘉其功，拜平章事，判三司。

translations.literal: Mingzong praised his achievement and appointed him Grand Councillor, with charge of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong rewarded him with the Grand Councillorship and charge of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 圜揀拔賢俊，杜絕幸門，百官俸入為孔謙減折。

translations.literal: Huan selected and promoted the worthy and talented, shut off the gates of favoritism; the salaries of the hundred officials had been reduced and discounted by Kong Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Huan promoted the worthy and closed the door to favoritism; Kong Qian had been cutting officials' salaries.

sentences.zh: 圜以廷臣為國家羽儀，故優假班行，禁其虛估，期月之內，府庫充贍，朝廷修葺，軍民鹹足。

translations.literal: Huan held that court ministers were the state's ceremonial plumes and banners, so he treated the official ranks generously and forbade inflated valuations; within a month the treasury was full, the court repaired, and army and people alike were provided for.
translations.idiomatic: Huan treated the court as the state's public face, forbade inflated valuations, and within a month the treasury was full, the palace restored, and army and people provided for.

sentences.zh: 雖憂國如家，而切於功名，故為安重誨所忌。

translations.literal: Though he grieved for the state as for his own household, he was keen on fame and achievement, and therefore was resented by An Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: Though he cared for the state as his own home, his hunger for glory made An Chonghui resent him.

sentences.zh: 嘗與重誨會於私第，有妓善歌，重誨求之不得，嫌隙自茲而深矣。

translations.literal: Once he met Chonghui at a private residence; there was a singing girl skilled in song whom Chonghui requested but could not obtain—the rift from this grew deep.
translations.idiomatic: Once at a private gathering a singer pleased Chonghui, who could not obtain her from Huan—their rift deepened from that day.

sentences.zh: 先是，使人食券，皆出於戶部，重誨止之，俾須內出，爭於御前，往復數四，竟為所沮，

translations.literal: Earlier, envoy ration vouchers all came from the Ministry of Revenue; Chonghui stopped this and required them to come from the inner palace; they disputed before the throne back and forth several times, and in the end Huan was obstructed,
translations.idiomatic: Envoy ration vouchers had come from the Ministry of Revenue; Chonghui required them from the inner palace instead; they argued back and forth before the throne four times, and Huan was blocked,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：安重誨與圜爭於上前，往復數四，聲色俱厲。

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: An Chonghui and Huan disputed before the throne back and forth several times, voice and countenance both fierce.
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian records that An Chonghui and Huan argued before the throne four times over, both fierce in voice and face.

sentences.zh: 上退朝，宮人問上：「適與重誨論事為誰？

translations.literal: When the emperor left court, a palace woman asked the emperor: "With whom was Chonghui just now discussing affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: After court a palace woman asked, "Who was arguing with Chonghui just now?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「宰相。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "The chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "The chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」宮人曰：「妾在長安宮中，未嘗見宰相、樞密奏事敢如是者，蓋輕大家耳！

translations.literal: " The palace woman said: "Your servant in the Chang'an palace never saw a chief minister or Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner report affairs daring to be like this—surely he looks down on the great house!"
translations.idiomatic: " She said, "In Chang'an I never saw a minister or military commissioner speak so boldly at audience—he must despise Your Majesty!"

sentences.zh: 」上愈不悅。）〉

translations.literal: " The emperor grew still more displeased.))
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor grew angrier still.))

sentences.zh: 因求罷三司。

translations.literal: He therefore requested to be relieved of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore asked to be relieved of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 天成二年，除太子少保致仕，出居磁州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiancheng he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and retired, going out to reside at Cizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiancheng 2 he retired as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and moved to Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 及朱守殷叛，重誨乘間誣其結構，立遣人稱製就害之，乃下詔曰：「太子少保致仕任圜，早推勳舊，曾委重難，既退免於劇權，俾優閑於外地，而乃不遵禮分，潛附守殷，緘題罔避於嫌疑，情旨頗彰於怨望。

translations.literal: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled, Chonghui seized the opportunity to accuse him of conspiracy, immediately sent a man bearing an edict to kill him on the spot, and then issued a proclamation: "Retired Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent Ren Huan was early esteemed as an old merit-holder and once entrusted with heavy difficulty; having been removed from intense power, he was granted ease in an outer region—yet he did not observe ritual propriety, secretly attached himself to Shouyin, sealed letters without avoiding suspicion, and his sentiments were quite manifest in resentment."
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Shouyin rebelled, Chonghui accused Ren of conspiracy and sent an agent with an edict to kill him at once, then proclaimed: "The retired Junior Guardian Ren Huan, once a meritorious minister entrusted in crisis, was granted ease abroad—yet he broke propriety, secretly aided Shouyin, exchanged letters without regard to suspicion, and his resentment was plain."

sentences.zh: 自收汴壘，備見蹤由，若務含宏，是孤典憲，尚全大體，止罪一身。

translations.literal: Since capturing the Bian stronghold, the tracks and causes have all been seen; if We insist on forbearance, We would abandon statutes and ordinances; still preserving the great framework, We punish only one person.
translations.idiomatic: Since Bian was taken the evidence is complete; to show forbearance would betray the law; preserving the larger order, We punish only him.

sentences.zh: 宜令本州於私第賜自盡。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order his home prefecture to grant him death by his own hand at his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: Let his prefect grant him death at his home.

sentences.zh: 」圜受命之日，聚族酣飲，神情不撓。

translations.literal: " On the day Huan received the order, he gathered his clan for hearty drinking; his spirit did not waver.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day the order came, he feasted with his clan and did not flinch.

sentences.zh: 清泰中，製贈太傅。

translations.literal: In Qingtai, by edict he was posthumously made Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai he was posthumously honored as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 子徹，仕皇朝，位至度支郎中，卒。

translations.literal: His son Che served the imperial court, reaching Director of the Revenue Section and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Che served the dynasty as Director of the Revenue Section and died in office.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：革、說承舊族之胄，佐新造之邦，業雖謝於財成，罪未聞於昭著，而乃為權臣之所忌，顧後命以無逃，靜而言之，亦可憫也。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Ge and Shuo bore the helmets of old clans and assisted a newly founded state; their achievements, though short of full completion, had crimes not heard to be manifest—yet they were resented by powerful ministers, and looking to the later command there was no escape; spoken of quietly, they may also be pitied.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Ge and Shuo came of old noble houses and served a newly founded dynasty; their work fell short of perfection, yet their crimes were hardly notorious—still powerful ministers hated them, and when the final sentence came they could not escape; calmly considered, they deserve pity.

sentences.zh: 盧程器狹如是，形渥攸宜。

translations.literal: Lu Cheng's capacity was so narrow—his form and favor were fittingly matched.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Cheng's talents were so meager—his rank suited his measure.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳、李愚，咸以文學之名，俱踐岩廊之位，校其貞節，愚復優焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Feng and Li Yu both by literary fame alike trod the cliffside galleries of state; comparing their integrity and constancy, Yu was again superior.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng and Li Yu both rose by literary fame to the council hall; in integrity Yu was the greater.

sentences.zh: 任圜有縱橫濟物之才，無明哲保身之道，退猶不免，籲可悲哉！

translations.literal: Ren Huan had talent to range widely and aid the world, but lacked the way of the wise in preserving himself—even in retirement he could not escape; alas, how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Ren Huan had the talent to serve the realm broadly but not the wisdom to save himself—even in retirement he could not escape; how lamentable!
